key_insight: Ordering and organizing training samples using pre-computed per-sample scores meaningfully changes LLM learning dynamics: simple sequence strategies (e.g., sort-by-quality or curriculum-style ordering) improve sample efficiency and final performance when models are trained for only a few epochs.
problem_solved: Addresses the underexplored challenge of how dataset ordering—beyond mere selection—affects LLM training efficiency and outcomes in low-epoch regimes, where a single pass or few passes over data dominate final model behavior.
method: Reuse pre-computed sample-level scores (quality, difficulty, uncertainty) as metadata for each example.
Systematically apply and compare organization strategies (sorted by score, curriculum/anti-curriculum, block vs. randomized shuffling) during training for 1–few epochs.
Measure impacts on convergence speed, validation performance, and downstream metrics to identify robust organization patterns.
impact: Provides a lightweight, practical lever for ML teams to improve training efficiency and model quality without extra data or heavy compute—especially useful for large models trained with limited epoch budgets.
visual_elements: Line chart: learning curves comparing random shuffle vs. sorted/curriculum order across 1–3 epochs.
Schematic pipeline: dataset + precomputed scores → reordering module → training loop (iconic boxes/arrows).
Bar chart: relative gains (accuracy/validation loss) for top organization strategies across tasks.
Icon set: clock (few epochs), funnel (data curation), sort icon (ordering), speedometer (efficiency)
paper_title: Demystifying Data Organization for Enhanced LLM Training
paper_authors: Yalun Dai, Yangyu Huang, Tongshen Yang, Yonghan Wang, Xin Zhang
